html:
The Guacata were a small Native people of southeast Florida, near the St. Lucie River and the Indian River Lagoon. They are known only from a few Spanish sources of the 1500s.

The main one is the memoir of Hernando de Escalante Fontaneda, who was shipwrecked in Florida in 1549 and lived among its peoples for seventeen years. Like their neighbours the Ais and the Jeaga, the Guacata likely lived by fishing, hunting and gathering, without farming. They fell under the power of the Calusa to the west. Disease and slave raids in the 1600s and 1700s destroyed them.
